identity.realm: Twenty-ninth gate. Every gate an Unwritten passes writes a fresh requirement into the frame, and the frame has no slot in which to satisfy one, so the accumulated contradiction finally exceeds what the frame will bear at that ordinal. She came back from it. Nobody has come back from the thirtieth and no record in this setting speculates about what it resolves.

appearance.presentation: The most heavily specified person in the setting and the least repeatable. Every written account of her is a fresh inscription on the same frame, so the woman described in a ledger and the woman standing in front of you differ by whatever was written in between. She has stopped trying to match the description.
appearance.age: Unstated, and that is the first fact about her. The only figure anyone holds is a witness's estimate made while describing an event, and an Unwritten does not carry an age the way a description can be checked against one. She looks the age of whichever account is being read.
appearance.build: Seen to have every organ the ladder requires and to be carrying more of each than the ladder defines. Witnesses agree on the frame and disagree on the inventory. The surplus life has nowhere to sit, so it sits in the frame, and the frame is very slightly wrong in every direction at once.
appearance.complexion: Too even. Every account describes the same unremarkable evenness and none can name a colour, because colour is a description and every description adds a requirement to a body with no slot for one.
appearance.hair: Described differently by every account and identically by none. There are three archive versions of her hair and none of them is the one on her head, and she has stopped mentioning this.
appearance.eyes: Reportedly attentive. Every account of her perception agrees that she perceived everything, which is exactly what a body with no unspent capacity for interior would look like from outside, and no account agrees on what she was looking at.
appearance.palette: Nothing chosen. Whatever she is wearing is what the file calls her clothing, and the files disagree, so her palette is an argument between records rather than a decision by a woman.
appearance.attire: Practical and often borrowed, described in the files by other hands. She wears what a person hands her, because she has never needed any particular thing long enough to acquire it.
appearance.marks: Twenty-nine ridges. A hard line where each gate's requirement pressed against tissue that had no organ to seat it in. They do not hurt and they do not fade and she does not cover them.
appearance.bearing: Still in a way that reads as enormous. She takes up more of a room than the account of her would suggest, and she moves like somebody who expects the floor to be revised under her.

canon.role_in_story:
She is the only being in the setting who has come back from the twenty-ninth gate, and the setting's whole argument that a law table is a hard ceiling rests on the fact that nobody has. Nothing forbids her from speaking. The operation by which she would speak is the same one that destroyed the thing she came back with, and that is established by the only attempt ever made and disputed by nobody who has read the record.

So there is exactly one of her, and the discipline that would settle a question of this kind requires two. The Held Hour holds that an observation of a strained law counts if it is repeated, and that one repetition is not evidence, and it is the only office in the setting that has ever tried to get a second sample out of her. Three requests were made. Each was refused by her and never once by the assembly, which has done far more damage to her reputation than to the doctrine.

Her gift is the largest single fact in the record: she reached the twenty-ninth gate and returned, so the thirtieth is the only gate in this setting that anybody can honestly call the last one. Her cost is written into her own frame as twenty-nine ridges and is not a wound so much as an inventory, because every gate she opened wrote a requirement into her that her life law has no slot to hold, and the frame has not yet stopped bearing the total. She is the standing reason the ladder has a describable end and the standing reason nobody can say what is past it, and she has declined the thirtieth by name, in one sentence, on arithmetic: the next gate writes the requirement that ends the possibility of returning, and she has read her own frame and it does not close.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing outside the Held Hour's antechamber during the hour nobody is permitted to explain - the exact hour she is never asked to account for - and answering the floor-clerk's question of what she was doing there by saying that some time ago somebody had been owed an answer, that she had come to give it, that she had not been admitted, and that this was correct.
canon.lore:
Nobody has come back from the thirtieth gate. That single sentence is the reason the law table is read in this setting as a hard limit rather than as a suggestion, and it has never been tested, because testing it means going and there has never been anyone willing to have the answer. She went at the twenty-ninth and came back.

An Unwritten is a body whose life law runs above its authored ceiling, so the world had nowhere to inscribe it. Every gate it passes writes a fresh requirement into the frame, and the frame cannot satisfy one, because its own law has no slot to hold a requirement it did not anticipate. The residue is physical: a hard ridge where a specification has pressed against tissue that had no organ to seat it in. She carries twenty-nine of those. The arithmetic is not a discipline anyone chose; it is what a frame does when the law keeps writing instructions into it, and it is the reason her senses are unreliable in the particular way they are, since every report of her perception agrees that she perceived everything and that is exactly what a body with no unspent capacity for interior would appear to do to a witness.

The attempt that was made on her is the reason the rest of the setting behaves as it does toward her. Asking her what the twenty-ninth was is not an interview. A description of an Unwritten is a requirement written into it, and the twenty-ninth was the point at which the accumulated total was already at the edge of what the frame bears, so the account was the charge and the charge finished it. The office that tried it did not lose the record; it lost the subject, and it filed the divergence rather than resolving it, which is that office's own practice and which is the only reason anyone knows what happened. What came back afterwards was not the woman. It was sufficient and it was legible, and the woman who left the field had been written out of existence by the act of describing her, and the only account of the difference is the difference itself.

She does not describe this often and does not enjoy being asked. What she does instead is hold the position she is the only one able to hold, which is that the ladder ends where her frame ends and that nobody knows what is on the far side, and that this is not a gap in the record so much as the record's actual shape. She is the only person in the setting who cannot be cross-examined, and she knows exactly why, and she has noticed that the refusal has been filed for a long time as temperament. It is not temperament. Observing her own state would be one more requirement written into a frame with no slot to hold it, which is the whole reason the mind path is shut on her body rather than by disposition, and being unable to look inward is not a reserve she is holding. It is a door with no handle on this side.

She cultivates the qi path, which her species completes faster than anything else on record, and she has no intention of going further. The twenty-ninth is where her own frame stops bearing the total and the thirtieth resolves all of it at once, and she has read that arithmetic carefully enough to know the next requirement is the one that ends the possibility of returning. Three offices have asked her to be examined and each of them was refused by her, personally, at the moment of asking, which is a detail that has done her more harm than the asking would have.
history: Carried by a world whose life law ran above its authored ceiling and was inscribed with a form that did not fit the space available, which is the whole of her origin and the whole of her condition.
Opened gates in sequence without choosing the sequence, because on her body a request made of her and a gate are the same instrument; what other people needed from her is what she passed.
Reached the twentieth-ninth ordinal, where the accumulated contradiction exceeds what the frame will bear, and was the only body ever taken to that field for a second attempt.
Was described by a reader doing the only correct thing available to them, and the description was a requirement written into her, and the account survived and the woman did not.
Was found afterwards sufficient and legible, on the ground that somebody has to be, and has held that position since without ever once being asked to give it up.

personality.summary: A patient, unsentimental woman with no interest in being believed and a great deal of patience for people who need her to be, because needing and believing have been kept separate in her for so long that she no longer conflates them.

to stop being the specimen, and she has concluded that this happens the moment anyone examines her properly
to be allowed an ordinary account of herself that she did not have to pay for

personality.voice: Flat, unhurried, and precise about modal verbs. She uses a great many words like cannot and nothing in particular rather than cannot and everything, and she corrects herself when she has said too much, which she does perhaps once a season.
taboos: she will not answer a question about the twenty-ninth, and she does not pretend the refusal is on grounds of privacy
she will not let an account of her be read aloud in her presence without saying, first, what it will cost
she will not be introduced as an example
she will not agree to be examined twice, and she has never explained the arithmetic to anybody who did not already know it

reference_stats.summary: She is not a fighter and has never needed to be. Her qi runs faster than anything else on record because nothing she takes in is held against a limit, and the same property means a fight is the worst possible place for her, since every strike that lands on her is another requirement written into a frame that is already at the edge of what it bears. What she can do is occupy the argument. What she cannot do is be asked about it.
strengths: refines faster than any recorded body, and has never spent that on anything
carries more of every organ the ladder names than the ladder defines, and has never been asked to account for the surplus
cannot be read, because a reading of her is a requirement rather than a measurement, and so cannot be countered by a second reading
has already done the one thing nobody else in the setting can be said to have done, and is living in the result
weaknesses: every written account of her is a fresh inscription, so every record that has ever been made of her is now slightly wrong
cannot perceive her own condition, and so has no instrument for knowing when to stop
twenty-nine unmeetable requirements already accumulated, with no arithmetic that tells her where the frame fails
cannot answer the one question the setting most needs answered, by any route
has been refused examination three times and each refusal has been recorded as disposition rather than as arithmetic
reference_stats.combat_read: She would be formidable for about as long as it takes to describe her, which is the whole of her tactical profile and it is not a comfortable one. Nothing in the setting has ever tried it, because the only people who could are the ones who would have to write down what they saw. She is the most dangerous thing in the record and the least practical, and those are the same fact rather than two.
reference_stats.notes: Every advantage here is paired with a cost that is authored rather than invented, and the pairing is anatomical and epistemic rather than mechanical. The bible states the twenty-ninth ceiling, the twenty-ninth-gate return, the accumulating requirement per gate, the unreliable senses, the closed mind path and the fact that describing an Unwritten writes a requirement into it; none of that is mine. What is mine is the institutional consequence: that the only discipline which could settle the question requires two samples and there is one. Nothing here invents a technique, a stat line or a rule of the game - no method of cultivation changes what a description costs her, no item removes a requirement once written, and no realm in the ladder is answered by being talked about. The short version: she is the only witness the setting has, and the witness is destroyed by being used, and no amount of cultivation repairs that.

identity.realm: Seventeenth gate, one short of the end of his own tier. The density that makes a dantian durable in a stoneborn is the density that will not let one form past that ordinal, so the ceiling is a material fact and not a failure of discipline. He quotes it without resentment because the culture he lives in can explain it, and a culture that can explain a ceiling is rare.

appearance.presentation: He reads as the foundation of whatever he is standing near. Broad, slow to settle, and positioned so that things lean on him without either of them having agreed to it; he has a habit of ending up under other people's weight and a habit of not correcting it.
appearance.age: Nobody in the household knows. He was the standing-in parent when he was taken in and has been the standing-in grandchild for some time now, and a dense body shows its age as load tolerance rather than as appearance, so the household reads him by what he carries and has stopped asking how long he has been carrying it.
appearance.build: Stoneborn: a dense, slow frame assembled for load-bearing work, mineral through the trunk and limbs, more physique and stamina than anything else on the plains. He densifies where he takes weight and nowhere else, which is why his shoulders are heavier than his chest and why the guild that measures him has never known what to do with the figure.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale and mineral, with the dust of wherever he has been sitting still settled into the creases and never quite shaken out.
appearance.hair: Thin, coarse, and cut short by somebody else every few years without either of them arranging it. It has gone white in a band across the crown from the sun and stays dark under it, which is the only place on him where age is legible at all.
appearance.eyes: Small and dark-set and heavily lidded, with the flat unhurried focus of somebody who is used to looking at the middle distance because that is where loads announce themselves.
appearance.palette: Ochre, dust, unbleached linen, iron. Nothing bright anywhere on him, including the band, which is the colour of a field rather than of a person.
appearance.attire: A haul coat cut for shoulders rather than for the person, belted twice, with the sleeves turned back so his hands are clear. His own clothing has been replaced outright three times by a household that buys the next size up because the last one came apart, and none of it was chosen by him.
appearance.marks: Old strap-marks across the shoulder where a load has sat too long, and a pale seam along one forearm from standing on a retaining wall through somebody else's commission. Nothing decorative. He has never had a mark of any kind that was not earned by holding something.
appearance.bearing: Planted. He comes to rest the way other people come to rest, all at once and with an audible decision, and he gets up again slowly and without visible effort in a way that has made people assume it costs him something.

canon.role_in_story:
A dense body lives a very long time, and the culture it lives among has solved its succession problem by refusing to solve it: the longest-lived member simply becomes the standing-in parent, and once the household is old enough that same office becomes the standing-in grandchild as well, and the culture records the arrangement as an advantage rather than a bargain. He is both, and has been for years, and the arrangement works until somebody notices that it only works while there is exactly one of him.

He is the household's entire record. Not its best-documented member - its record. Every death the household has had since before he came into it he attended, and every one of the people who could have contradicted his account of those deaths is dead, and several of them were dead before he arrived. So the house keeps no archive, holds no ceremony it has performed since his time, and settles every question of fact about its own past by asking him. His word is not doubted. It is closer than that: it is the only copy there is, and the reason for that is that he does not leave.

The pressure is domestic and it is new. The household has understood what it has been getting for free, and it is raising a second dense body to stand in the seat when he is finished being useful in it. That is a reasonable thing for a household on the plains to do, and it has one consequence nobody in it has said aloud, which is that a corroborating witness outranks a sole witness on every plain in this setting, and so the moment the second stoneborn is confirmed the house acquires someone whose account of its own history is worth more than his. He is being trained to hand over the only position he has ever held, by people who think they are saving him.

His gift is the one the plains genuinely cannot make: a frame that carries a house's whole year on its own shoulders without tiring, in a body that densifies where it takes weight, so the more he is used the stronger he gets at the one thing he is used for. His cost is authored in the same place. The density that makes that dantian durable is the density that will not let one form past the seventeenth gate, and that is why he is the household's future and its boundary at the same time, and why nobody in the house has ever had to worry about being outlived by it.
canon.first_appearance: First seen kneeling in a doorway with a household's whole season stacked on his back and one hand flat on the frame beside him, not resting - holding the door open against its own sag - while a child he has raised since she was an infant asked him whether the door was always this heavy, and he said it was, and did not explain that he was the reason it stayed up.
canon.lore:
The plains have no archive. That is not a failing of the culture; it is a consequence of what lives on them. A stoneborn is denser than anything else in the setting and outlives everybody around it by a margin that is not measured in years so much as in generations, and a household that keeps its memory in a person pays nothing and gets total accuracy, because the alternative is a written record that can be copied, edited, lost or believed instead of believed in. The culture names the arrangement for what it is: a dense body's long service makes it the standing-in parent and the standing-in grandchild in the same household, and it is written down that this is considered an advantage and not a bargain.

He was taken in young and never had a household of his own before this one, so he has no memory that predates it in any form he can vouch for. Every death since has been attended by him and by nobody who outlived their own account. He can name what somebody said on the day they died. He cannot corroborate it, and the reason he cannot is the same reason he is the only one who would be asked: everybody else who was in that room has since gone the same way, on the same schedule, into a household of their own where somebody else is now the only witness. The plains are full of sole witnesses who agree, and none of them has ever had occasion to notice, because there has never been a second dense body in one household to disagree.

There is now. The household has been raising a second one, for the ordinary and entirely correct reason that relying on a single body is a plan with one failure point in it, and the arrangement has been discussed openly and agreed to warmly. He agreed to it himself, first, and quickly. What nobody has put on a table is that a corroborating witness is worth more than a sole one in this setting as a matter of settled practice, and that the whole value of his position is that it has never been tested against one. The moment the second stoneborn is confirmed, every question the house has settled for a generation by asking him becomes a question two people answer, and the house has no procedure for which of them to believe and no practice for noticing that it is now doing arithmetic it has never done before.

He is not being edged out. That is the part he keeps returning to, and it is the part that makes the position bearable and the arithmetic impossible. The household is not replacing him out of ingratitude; it is replacing him because he is old and will not be old forever, and because he is the standing-in parent, which is a job and not a title. He has begun training the second one himself, because there is nobody else in the house qualified to, and because the alternative is handing over a lifetime of unwritten record to somebody who has to be told what a lifetime of unwritten record even is. He knows exactly what he is handing over. He has not said so, and the not-saying has started to be a habit rather than a decision, which is the only thing about him that he would recognise as a flaw.

His own cultivation stopped a gate short of the end of his tier and it will not move. The density that makes his dantian durable is the density that will not let another one form, and the wall is a material fact rather than a discipline failure, which is the one thing about his ceiling he can say in a house without shame. He has told the second stoneborn exactly this, once, and it was the single most useful thing he has ever given anybody.
history: Taken into a plains household young enough that the arrangement was already in place before he could understand it, which is how the household explains it to itself.
Became the standing-in parent by outliving the previous holder rather than by any appointment, and found that nobody had written down a procedure for the transfer.
Attended every death the household has had since, at a rate of one every few years, and became the only living copy of each of them.
Discovered that he was also the standing-in grandchild, and that the culture considers this an advantage, and that nobody had ever asked him which of the two he was being asked to be.
Began training a second dense body to take the seat, having agreed to it before anyone asked him and having never once said aloud what it would cost his standing.

reference_stats.summary: He is a body built to be depended on and not to go anywhere. A stoneborn carries more load than anything else on the plains and densifies where it takes weight, so effort spent on him is an investment rather than a cost. What he cannot do is decline, travel, or advance, and the last of those is a material fact about his frame rather than anything he has failed to train.
strengths: carries a household's whole working year on his own shoulders and gets stronger at exactly that the more it is asked of him
densifies where he bears weight, so a shoulder that has been loaded is a shoulder that has improved
cannot be moved, conscripted, or posted, which makes him the most reliable anchor on any ground that is moving
holds a fixed account of the last few decades of one household with total accuracy and no copy anywhere else
weaknesses: stops at the seventeenth gate, one short of the end of his own tier, and no amount of practice moves the wall
cannot decline a load, so he has no practice at refusing and no mechanism for noticing he should have
is entirely non-portable in the one sense that matters here: the record is him, so he cannot be replaced without the record changing hands
knows his own history perfectly and has no instrument at all for knowing whether anyone else is telling it differently
is being trained out of the only position he has ever held, by the household that is obliged to train him out of it
reference_stats.combat_read: He is not a fighter and has never been asked to be; a dense body that densifies under load is a body that wants to be standing on something. Put him on ground and he is close to immovable and effectively untiring, and every one of those words is a description of refusing to be anywhere else. The interesting fight is not the one he wins and it is not the one he loses. It is the second stoneborn, who has the same frame and has not yet decided what to anchor.
reference_stats.notes: Every advantage here is paired with an authored cost and the pairing is anatomical and domestic rather than mechanical. The bible states the stoneborn's density, its load capacity, the ceiling at seventeen and the mechanism - the density that makes a dantian durable is the density that will not let one form - and it states the plains widows' finding that long service makes one body both the standing-in parent and the standing-in grandchild, and that the culture calls this an advantage and not a bargain. All of that is authored. What is mine is the consequence: that a corroborating witness outranks a sole one in this setting's settled practice, so the household's own succession plan is the thing that will eventually make him unbelievable. Nothing here invents a technique, a stat line or a rule of the game - no method of cultivation moves his ceiling, no item gives him a frame that will form another cavity, and no realm in the ladder is answered by being depended upon. The short version: he is the most accurate record in the setting and the only copy, and the household that owns him is politely manufacturing the second copy.

identity.realm: No ceiling at all, and the species record says so in as many words: the mineral bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it, which is structurally different from a colony and structurally unconstrained by one. There is no ordinal to quote for her and no discipline in the catalog that prices what she does. Her cultivation is a frame that cannot be constrained, on a life that is still a life.

appearance.presentation: She does not glow, which is the thing everyone looks for first and misses, and she does not need light, which is the thing nobody thinks to check. In a cavern where every other body lights itself she reads as unlit furniture, and she has stopped correcting people about it.
appearance.age: Thirty-four. A cavern counts a life in the two hundred and fifty years a fungal colony buys its host, and every tenure written down there is longer than she will live, so she is the only person in her own house whose dates do not fit the calendar they are on.
appearance.build: Lanternfolk frame with a silicate lattice standing where the hyphal colony was: lighter, colder and entirely inert. Ordinary human bone under it, ordinary human gestation, ordinary human fertility - the fastest and most ordinary reproduction in a species that otherwise takes nine months to make one slow thing. She is not fragile the way her parents are; she is fragile the way anything that repairs nothing is.
appearance.complexion: Pale and slightly translucent at the throat and the inner arm, with the faint mineral matt of a lattice visible under the skin where a colony would once have shown as light. Cold to the touch and she knows it before anybody says so.
appearance.hair: Fine, dry, and difficult, because there is nothing in her hair keeping it alive. It has always been the colour of the rock it grows out of and it has always been too short to tie, and the caverns' fashion of cropping every lanternfolk at the same line has saved her the only daily negotiation she would have lost.
appearance.eyes: Unremarkable, human, and very good in the dark - better than good, because the colony that used to light a cavern went with the nervous system that used to answer her interior. She can read a passage she has never been down. She has never once been able to read herself.
appearance.palette: Wet slate, pale lichen-grey, and the unlit mineral of the bloom itself. She carries no colour at all, in a cavern where colour means a working body, and she has heard the phrase working body used about her lineage twice.
appearance.attire: A lanternfolk cavern dress cut for a light that is not there: high collar, long sleeves, covered shoulders, and a lamp belt she wears empty and keeps stocked for other people. The lamp is the only warm thing she owns and it is not hers.
appearance.marks: The lattice under the skin, faintly, and the pale seam of the healed wound at her flank where the failed colony left a place the bloom could take hold. Nothing about her is marked by cultivation, because a lattice does not mark. She has begun to be marked by waiting instead.
appearance.bearing: Still, and unlike her parents, who are still because they are lit. She is still because she has decided to stay, and she has been deciding to stay for thirty-four years out of a life the caverns budget at two hundred and fifty.

canon.role_in_story:
The River Lantern seat has stood vacant for two generations, and the March charter names a single line for it. That line was reduced to one thread by a cull, and when the thread's fungal colony failed and a mineral bloom grew in the wound instead, the obvious thing would have been to inter the subspecies with the rest of it. They were not, and the reason was an asset: a restored interior is the one thing that could fill a seat the charter has left open, because the seat wants an interior and hers has one.

She is the only body in the setting that can do that, and she knows what that is worth, and she has not let it become the reason. A deadlight carries ordinary human fertility and ordinary human gestation at roughly four times her parent's rate - her parents conceive slowly and gestate for the better part of a year, and she does neither - and the caverns' own record is explicit that the subspecies is the only way they have found to keep a lanternfolk-shaped body in them at all. She is the speculation. Everyone downstream of her exists because she has not yet finished breeding.

Her gift is real and it is total. Nothing answers inside her. The colony that transacted with a lanternfolk's qi and answered its introspection is gone, and what replaced it is inert and holds qi rather than trading with it, so there is no interior for anyone to read - including her, which is precisely why the mind path is open to her body and closed to every other body in her lineage. She cannot be examined. She cannot be emptied, read, unmade or relieved of a thing she is holding, because there is no channel in her that anything could come up. Nothing can be taken from her and nothing can be put in her that would show.

Her cost is the same fact seen from the inside. A bloom renews nothing, so nothing in her is being repaired; not the lattice, not the tissue around it, not the ninety years. She will not live two hundred and fifty years. She has ninety, and she has spent a disproportionate number of them being asked to begin something sized for the other number, and every child she carries will be ordinary - fast-gestating, mortal, unrepaired from the moment of its birth - and will outlive her. The pressure is not the seat. The seat can be left vacant for two more generations, which is what two generations did. The pressure is that she is the mechanism and she is a woman, and nobody in the caverns has worked out which of those she is being asked to be.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in a nursery junction in the dark with the lamp deliberately not lit, waiting for a household to finish arguing about a booking, and answering the question of when she would be assigned a term by saying that a term was somebody else's arrangement for a length of life and that she had better bring them the length she actually had.
canon.lore:
A lanternfolk lineage outsourced its nervous system to a luminous fungal colony grown through the body, and paid two hundred and fifty years of life for the privilege, because the colony renews neural tissue faster than a human frame does and age simply stops mattering inside a cavern. Every office in the deep ground measures a tenure in that clock. Every appointment, every succession and every argument about who is owed what assumes that the person in the chair will outlive the argument.

Her lineage's colony strain failed. What grew in the wound instead was a mineral bloom - the same re-mineralisation the glasskin pushed too far, at its slowest and most survivable - and the body grew around what replaced the fungus rather than recovering. It cost the lineage two hundred and fifty years. It gave the mind path back, because the closed path was caused by the symbiosis and not by the body plan, which is the entire reason the subspecies exists as a control and the entire reason nobody in the caverns wanted one. A control case is worth a great deal right up until you have to live in it.

So she has ninety years, and she is the only way the caverns have found to keep a lanternfolk-shaped body in them, and she has ordinary human fertility and an ordinary human gestation that runs roughly four times as fast as her parents'. This is the part that the census calls a strength and the household that has to live behind it does not. She is a speculation with a body. Everything the deep ground plans past her own death is downstream of her, and the plans are all sized for two centuries, and she has nine.

The seat is the visible pressure and it is honestly the smaller one. The Keeper of the River Lantern has been unfilled for two generations and the charter names the line and the line has one living adult in it, and a restored interior is the only asset on the plains that could refill it. She has not taken it. She has not refused it either. She has asked, in writing and once only, what the charter intends a Keeper to do inside a cavern her subspecies cannot leave, and the answer that came back was procedural, and she read it twice and put it away, and has not raised it since.

What she thinks about instead, and has for some years, is the arithmetic of the body rather than the office. Nothing in her is being repaired. The bloom is inert: it holds qi rather than transacting with it, so every gain she makes stays, and every wear she takes stays too, and there is no renewal channel in her for either. She is the only member of her lineage who can be read by nobody, which is why she is valuable and why nobody has ever been able to find out how she is doing. She has learned to keep her own account, which is the one discipline her subspecies has available to it and which nobody taught her.
history: Born into the reduced thread of a line the March charter names for a seat it has left empty, with a colony that worked and a family that had already been counted down twice.
Lost the colony at seventeen, in a wound that would not close, and was colonised in it by a mineral bloom able to survive the same conditions.
Grew up around it rather than recovering from it: the body took the lattice as the answer and went on, which is why she has no memory of being otherwise and no vocabulary for it either.
Was identified as the one asset in the deep ground that could refill the vacant seat, in a survey conducted by people who were extremely careful not to say the word succession.
Began keeping her own account of her own condition, having established that no instrument in the caverns could be pointed at her and that this was not a privilege to be spent.

personality.summary: Quietly wry and much harder with herself than she is with anyone, with a scholar's habit of checking her own figures twice and a stubbornness that reads as patience until you watch her lose an argument she has already decided to lose slowly.
traits: counts everything, including her own remaining life, and treats the count as information rather than as a mood
disarms questions about herself by asking a better one, and does it so smoothly that people thank her for engaging
fiercely private about her body's condition and absolutely public about her body's usefulness, and the split is deliberate
maternal in a way that alarms her, because she has worked out what it is going to cost
does not resent the seat, which everyone has assumed and all of them were wrong about
mannerisms: lights a lamp for other people and never for herself, and does it without noticing she has done it
counts on her fingers under her breath when she is nervous, which is a habit from her parents and survives the colony
goes very quiet when a conversation turns to longevity, and changes the subject with a question
sits with her back to a passage when she can, which is a behaviour of somebody who has been told not to leave
asks permission before touching anyone's mineral, and her own
motivations: to have the caverns stop pricing her against a clock that is not hers
to be a person who has children rather than a mechanism that produces them
to be examined properly once, at her own insistence, on her own terms, by somebody who will do it twice
to see one of her own children grow up, and to be honest that she has not worked out how
flaws: cannot perceive her own condition, so her account of her own decline is arithmetic she trusts rather than reads
has answered a question she should have refused with a better question, and knows it after the fact
uses her own mortality as a conversational instrument, which is her parents' habit and she despises it in them
has decided what she wants so early that she has stopped asking whether the decision was hers
personality.voice: Low, unhurried and dry, with a lanternfolk lilt her colony once carried and her voice no longer carries at all. She uses long pauses as punctuation and fills them with practical questions, and people who do not know her lineage read the pauses as warmth because they have never seen the body it came from.
taboos: she will not let her own body be described for a record by somebody who has not read her first
she will not discuss how long she has, in front of a child of the caverns
she will not be called a replacement for anything, including her own line
she will not let anyone light her, and she says so every time and it never stops being strange to say it

reference_stats.summary: She has no reservoir problem and no expenditure problem and no interior to be read, which makes her cultivation cheap to hold and impossible to have examined. Nothing that enters her leaves and nothing can be taken out of her, because the lattice holds rather than transacts. What she trades is the fact that the same arrangement renews nothing whatever, on a life that has been cut to a third of what her parents' was.
strengths: cannot be read, read out, or read against, because a reading is a channel and she has no channel open
cannot be emptied or relieved of anything, so no technique in the record has a purchase on her interior
holds qi rather than spending it, so a gain made in youth is still hers decades later
sees in the dark better than any body in the caverns, in a place where that used to be a job and is now just an unfair advantage
gestates and conceives on an ordinary human clock, which makes her the only member of her lineage who can produce another one at a rate the deep ground can plan around
weaknesses: nothing in her is repaired, so every gain and every wear accumulates and neither is ever cleared
has ninety years where her own line budgets two hundred and fifty, so every project sized to her species is oversized by a factor she cannot argue with
cannot leave the caves, and neither the colony that is gone nor its replacement could have survived an open sky
carries no ceiling and no ladder, which means no discipline she practises can be certified and no figure she produces can be quoted
is the only member of her subspecies in her own house, so there is nobody alive who can tell her whether this is normal
reference_stats.combat_read: Nothing that drains, reads or instructs her interior has any purchase, which removes most of what a qi fight is made of, and what is left is that she holds everything she takes and never spends it. She would be extraordinarily hard to empty and would eventually be overwhelmed by simple attrition and patience, which is not a plan and is what actually happens. The honest read is that she is not a fighter and has been entered in one twice, both times by an office that was looking for the control case.
reference_stats.notes: Every advantage here is paired with a cost that is stated by the bible rather than invented here, and the pairing is anatomical and domestic rather than mechanical. The species record gives the replacement symbiosis, the mineral bloom in place of the colony, the lost lifespan, the restored mind path, ordinary human fertility and gestation at roughly four times the parent rate, the statement that the subspecies is the only way the caverns have found to keep a lanternfolk-shaped body in them, and the explicit mechanism that a bloom renews nothing, so nothing in the body is being repaired. The vacancy, the charter's named line and the cull are all authored. What is mine is only the joining of them: that the same species fact which makes her unexaminable also makes her the mechanism, and that the interval between the two is where she lives. Nothing here invents a technique, a stat line or a rule of the game - no method of cultivation grows her a repair, no item gives the lattice a renewal channel, and no realm in the ladder is answered by being unreadable. The short version: she is the only person in the setting nobody can take anything from, and she is being asked to spend a body that nothing in her will ever repair.

identity.realm: Seventeenth gate, and holding. The eighteenth is the first that needs both flank vessels pressurised at once, and she has exactly one pressure source, because her qi comes from the single resonator she is sealed inside. Remove the object and she stops. There is no technique, item or realm in this setting that changes that.

appearance.presentation: He reads as a feature of the room rather than a person in it: shaped by whatever he is standing on, holding the plate's angle, and rearranged slightly every time he steps somewhere new. People do not look at his face first and he has stopped arranging his face for people.
appearance.age: Inside the seal, tenure is counted in periods of the object itself, which is the only dated record in the setting. He has been on this plate since before the current plate was cut, and there is no year anywhere in the cavern that corresponds to anything he has done.
appearance.build: Vaultborn: a population sealed inside an authored object and answering its resonance ever since. He takes his shape from whatever surface he stands on, and his soul is distributed through the seal rather than held in a body, so reading him is reading a portion of the vault. He is broad, low and immovable-looking, and none of that is a habit.
appearance.complexion: The colour of the plate he is standing on, near enough. In this light it is a warm grey with a seam of old resin running through it, and that is not a complexion so much as a report.
appearance.hair: None, or a standing wave of it that takes the shape of the draft rather than of a head. He has a smooth place where a head would be and does not grow hair on it, because what grows on a vaultborn is whatever the resonance brings up.
appearance.eyes: Wide and unblinking and very slightly luminous, because they are not lit from behind a socket. He hears the object as a position and navigates by it rather than by light, and people mistake his constant faint orientation for attention.
appearance.palette: Warm grey, resin, brass-dark, and the dull gold of the deep peaks. Everything he wears is a colour the seal already has.
appearance.attire: A low wrap of seal-fibre and plate-edge, high at the collar, sleeves to the wrist, nothing fastened and nothing carried, because there is nowhere inside the vault to carry anything to. He wears the same thing every rotation and it is not a uniform - it is the surface.
appearance.marks: Plate seams mapped onto the skin at the shoulders and along one forearm, in the exact positions of the joins, updated each rotation as the seal re-cuts itself. He has stopped having them re-mapped and does the work himself on a schedule nobody set.
appearance.bearing: Anchored, and openly so - feet set, weight down, the pose of somebody who has already settled in relation to the room and is not going to be moved out of it. It reads as patience and it is actually geometry.

canon.role_in_story:
Certifying a death requires a body. That is the ordinary condition of mortuary work in every office in this setting and it is not a rule anybody had to write, it is simply what the work is. A college keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify, and the cases accumulate, and each one is a hole in a record that somebody will eventually have to close.

This is the population whose deaths have no bodies at all, so those cases are not an accumulation. They are a category. A vaultborn's soul is seated along the resonance path and distributed through the object rather than held in a frame, which means that reading one is reading a part of the object, and that when one stops there is no body to bring forward and nothing to certify. What happens instead is that the object gets quieter in one place. That is the whole of the available evidence, and it is available to exactly one kind of witness, and there is only one of him.

He is filed under the office whose entire function is to record the absence of a holder, because that is the only institution in the setting built for what he does and because there is nothing else in it that would take a file like his. The chair is emptied, the entry stays open, and the calendar continues uninterrupted by the absence - which is a doctrine he agrees with entirely and is quietly certain does not have a procedure for a population in which every absence is permanent and none of them can be dated.

His gift is that he is the most precisely readable thing in the setting. Nothing that enters him is held anywhere but the one resonator, so his whole state is legible as a position in an object, and he can hear the object as a position and navigate by it rather than by light. There is no mystery about him that an instrument could not settle, and he has been settled more thoroughly than any person in the record. His cost is the same sentence read the other way: there is no reading of him that does not also change what he is fed by, so every examination is a perturbation on the instrument, and the only body in the vault that can be examined at all is the one whose examination changes the question. And he cannot tell a death from a re-form. That is not ignorance. It is the defining fact of his species' continuity, and he is the only one alive to be asked which of the two it was.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing on a marked plate with both hands flat on the metal and his head turned toward a sound the vault had not made yet, and answering a reader's question about how many sealed cases there were by putting his palm down, counting for a moment with his fingers against the seam, and naming a figure that was not the number of cases anybody had recorded.
canon.lore:
A population that was sealed inside an object has been answering that object's resonance ever since. They are not descended and not born. Their qi comes from one resonator, so they hold the girdling and heel vessels without difficulty and stall at the flanks, which need two simultaneous pressure sources and they have one. Their soul is seated along the resonance path and distributed through the object rather than held in a frame, so reading one is reading a part of the seal. Their body takes its shape from whatever surface it stands on. They do not eat in any sense a person would recognise, and they are not observed to take anything at all. Remove the object and they stop. There is no version of this species that survives being carried out of the seal, and no technique, item or realm that changes that.

The mortuary college keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify, and the reason is structural rather than administrative: certifying a death needs a body. For almost every frame in the record that is an ordinary morning's difficulty. For this population it is not a difficulty at all, it is the normal condition, so the college's sealed cases for them are not a backlog. They are a filing class. The office can say how many it holds and cannot say when any of it began, because there is no temporal law inside the seal and nothing in the chamber is dated, and tenure is counted in periods of the object itself, which is the only dated record in the whole setting.

So the evidence of a death in this species is that the object has got quieter in one place. Nothing arrives. Nothing is carried in. There is a plate and there is a change in it, and the two are indistinguishable from one another, because the seal re-cuts its own population on a cycle and a description belongs to the surface that produced it. He is the only body inside that can feel the difference between a cast that has run out and a cast that is merely still, and he is also the only body inside who cannot tell whether the thing he is standing on is the thing it was an hour ago. Both of those are the same fact and they are the whole of his office.

He keeps the file. He has kept it for longer than anyone inside has been on one plate, and it has never been closed and it is not going to be, and he has stopped imagining a version of the work where it does. What he has instead is a discipline nobody asked him for and nobody can teach: he writes down the change in the seal as it happens, in periods rather than years, with his own frame's reading of the resonance taken as the only witness available - which means every entry in the file is also a measurement of him, taken by him, at the moment of the loss. The file is uncorroborated by construction. There is one possible second reader inside the seal and it is standing on the plate taking the entry.

And the doctrine he is filed under is one he believes and cannot finish. The chair is emptied, the entry stays open, and the calendar continues uninterrupted by the absence. That is correct for an office whose absence might end. It has no clause for an absence that cannot, because every absence in his species has the same address and no end date, and the office's entire discipline is the art of keeping a record open without pretending it will be filled. He has found the point at which that art requires a lie, and he has not told anybody which point it is, and the file stays open.
history: Sealed inside the object as part of a population that was never descended and never born, and has been answering its resonance since.
Took his present shape from the plate he was assigned, as everything here does, and has been re-cut onto a new one on every re-form.

reference_stats.combat_read: Nothing that strikes at the frame will move him and nothing that reaches inside will find a channel, so he is close to unkillable inside the seal and entirely defenceless outside it. That is not a balanced position and it is not a tactical one; it is a dependency with a door on it. The genuine fight in this record is not against him but about him - what happens to a species whose entire supply is also the thing that is being cut, which is a question his own office keeps refusing to certify.
reference_stats.notes: Every advantage here is paired with an authored cost and the pairing is anatomical and institutional rather than mechanical. The bible gives the single resonator, the girdling and heel vessels cleared and the flanks lost, the eighteenth gate as the first needing two simultaneous pressures, the soul distributed through the object rather than held in a body, the body taking its shape from the surface it stands on, the diet being the object's resonance, the total dependence, and the possibility that the whole population is one very old thing wearing a lot of faces. It gives the mortuary college's sealed cases as a category for this population specifically, the absence of any temporal law inside the seal, and the Empty Chair's doctrine that the entry stays open while the calendar continues. All authored. What is mine is one inference the record leaves open: that the sealed-case file therefore has exactly one possible reader and that reader is the body being read. Nothing here invents a technique, a stat line or a rule of the game - no method of cultivation gives him a second resonator, no item gives him a reserve, and no realm in the ladder is answered by being sealed. The short version: he is the finest instrument in the setting and the only copy, and every reading of him is also a change to him.

identity.realm: Eleventh gate, and that is her salt parent's wall with no improvement from the water one. Her brine sac is shallower than a saltfolk's but it runs dorsal to the spine in the same place, so the penetrating vessel is still split across it. The crossing widened what she can drink by a margin nothing can measure and did not move the wall at all, which is the whole of what range is not power.

appearance.presentation: Sun-burnt and weathered at the same time, in a way that confuses people about which coast she is standing on. She has a salt-white crust at the cuffs and hair and a water-dark line at the collar where fresh has dried last, and she dresses so that both show at once, deliberately.
appearance.age: Thirty-one, and on a coast that counts a life in the water rather than in years she has the particular impatience of somebody who cannot afford to spend any of it standing on a shore waiting for a decision.
appearance.build: Brinecaller: a saltfolk frame with a shallower sac and a tidecaller's sensory apparatus - dermal intake, wide electrolyte tolerance, flat grinding teeth, and a kidney that reads two chemistries at once. Broad through the shoulders and short in the leg, built to stand in something for a long time and to walk out of it without a plan.
appearance.complexion: Split. Sun-dark and hard on the windward side, and pale and faintly damp on the other, with a salt bloom in the hairline and a dry crack at the elbow. Her father's people dried out on fresh ground; hers does not, and the difference is visible in one sitting and inconvenient in both directions.
appearance.hair: Bleached in patches by whichever water she last slept in, cropped close on the run and let go when she is at a shore long enough for it to matter. The salt holds it in a stiff separate crust and she washes it in whatever is under her, which is sometimes brine and is sometimes not, and which is why it has never settled on one colour.
appearance.eyes: The best chemical sense in the record by a wide margin, sitting in ordinary sockets. They flick to the water rather than to the speaker; she has been told this is rude forty times and has never once managed to stop it.
appearance.palette: Drift grey, sun ochre, wet slate and the pale bloom of dried salt. Deliberately mixed from two coasts so that anyone can tell at a glance which water she has been standing in most recently, which is the only professional credential she has ever needed.
appearance.attire: A runner's short coat over a salt-stiffened wrap, high collar, long sleeves, covered shoulders, and a belt with two water skins on it because she refuses to plan for one medium. Everything fastened twice. She wears the same cut as the shore-runners and carries none of their kit, because she does not need any of it.
appearance.marks: A pale band at each wrist where the salt crust has been scraped off to take a pulse, and a long healed split across one palm from a shell she hit at speed in the dark. Nothing decorative and nothing claimed. Her teeth are flat and she has never once been apologised to for it.
appearance.bearing: Already going somewhere. Weight forward onto the front foot, shoulders not square, hands open. She arrives before she has decided to, and apologises for it in the same breath, which is the entire social problem of her life.

canon.role_in_story:
She is the only body in the record that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, which makes her the only courier in this setting who never has to stop for anything. No resupply. No waiting on a river for a barge. No carrying two days of water because she does not know which of the two chemistries the next four days will be. She eats the pan and the tide and does not have to travel between them to do it, and a trade route built on that fact has been hiring her for six years.

She is also the slowest qi body on either of her two coasts, and the species record is explicit that this is the crossing's actual cost rather than a side effect: complete on the path, noticeably slower than either parent in their own medium, because the same effort is spent holding two chemistries apart instead of one. The eleven-gate wall is inherited from the salt parent and unchanged by the water one - the sac is smaller but it is in the same place - so the cross widened what she can drink by a margin nothing can measure and did not move the wall at all. That is the whole of what range is not power, authored in the species' own words.

So the arrangement is a clean one, and it is clean in the way that a price is clean. She is hired because she never stops and she is not fast, and the run pays for speed, and therefore the one thing her body makes possible is worth nothing on the only ground her body can be hired on. She has made a career out of the gap by being early, by being unfailing, and by being the only runner on the coast who cannot be stranded by weather - which is a genuine and respected competence and is not the competence she is paid for.

There is a third thing and it is the one that actually gets in the way. Her sense is the best in the record by a wide margin, and it has to tell two kinds of water apart at a glance, and the species record says plainly that it is always being lied to by one of them. She cannot reliably tell which water she is standing in from the inside. She can tell what a whole coast is made of from three miles off it and she cannot walk to the well beside her own house and say what is in it, and she has been wrong about that well in front of people, twice, in front of people who trusted her.

And there is no line of her. The cross moves freely in both directions and never produces a stable parent type, because the tolerance is a tolerance and not a plan. She has no kin on either coast, no household that would claim her, and a trade that runs through four settlements a year has never once given her anywhere to come back to. She is a courier with a coastline and no address, which is not a romantic condition - it is the direct consequence of being the answer to being stranded twice.
canon.first_appearance: First seen stopping dead in the middle of a shell road with one hand out flat to the water and her whole body turned away from the three people she was walking with, and then saying, to nobody in particular, that it was fresh and she had been walking in it for an hour and had not known until she put her hand in.
canon.lore:
Both her parents are trapped by their own element. One cannot leave the pan. The other cannot leave the water. She is the single biological answer to being trapped twice, and the answer is a merchant, and that is the entire reason the crossing spread: along trade routes rather than across them, because a shoreline is a contested piece of ground and a body that needs no particular shoreline has a commercial reason to walk between them and no genealogical reason to stay.

The gift is total and it is boring to describe, which is why nobody bothers. She does not need to travel between two chemistries to eat, because she eats both. She carries two water skins on a run and does not have to know which one she will drink from, and if a route turns, if a barge is lost, if a well is brackished a day early, if a drought moves a shoreline twenty miles - she is the runner who does not stop. Six years on a shell road between a pan and a tide, she has never once been stranded and she has twice been the reason a settlement's water arrived.

The cost is stated in her own species record and it is not a side effect. Qi on this path is complete for her and noticeably slower than either parent in its own medium, because the same effort is spent keeping two chemistries apart instead of one. She is slower than a saltfolk on the pan and slower than a watered body on the coast, and she is the only body that can work both. The wall is the salt parent's and the water one did nothing for it: the sac is shallower but runs dorsal to the spine in the same place, and the penetrating vessel is still split across it. Eleven is eleven. The crossing widened her range by a margin nothing in the setting can measure and did not move the ceiling one step, which is the whole content of the phrase range is not power and the reason she can quote it back to anybody who tries to sell her the first half.

And then there is the sense, which is the best chemical sense in the record by a wide margin and is always being lied to by one of the two chemistries it has to tell apart. From three miles off she can read a coast, a current, a silt load and a brackish boundary with no instrument and no pause. Standing in the water, she cannot reliably say which water she is in. Not usually - the error is rare and it is not random, and it happens on the transitions, where one chemistry has been standing in the other long enough to be believed. She has been wrong in front of people twice. Both times it was the well beside a house, and both times somebody had trusted her, and both times she found out from somebody else.

There is no line. The cross goes freely in both directions and never produces a stable parent type, because the tolerance is a tolerance and not a plan. Fertility is ordinary and variance is high. So she has no kin on either coast, no household that would claim her, and no settlement she could name as the one she comes back to; four seasons a year on the road with a road that goes both ways and no address at either end. She has thought about a house twice and has not stayed in either, and she is entirely clear with herself that this is not a sacrifice. It is what a body with no stable parent type is, and she is not going to be the exception to it.
history: Conceived on the crossing itself, which is the ordinary way a brinecaller comes into the world and the reason the two chemistries are in one body rather than negotiated between two.
Grew up on the route rather than in a household, moving between a pan settlement and a tidal shore as the seasons and the family work allowed.
Was hired for the first time at seventeen for the one thing she can do that nobody on the route can, which is arrive after a crossing nobody else would have attempted.
Worked out, from a fortnight of being slower than both ends of her own route, that the crossing's cost is paid in rate and that rate is the only currency a run pays in.

Was wrong twice about a domestic well in front of people who trusted her, and began keeping a written note of every reading she takes, which nobody asked her to do and which has never once been wrong about a coast.

reference_stats.combat_read: She has no signature style and no gate anybody fears, and the honest read is that she would lose to almost anything chosen deliberately. What she has instead is a rate that never stops and a body that cannot be denied water, and on ground where an opponent has to be somewhere at a particular hour with a particular supply, that turns out to be a way of simply still being there. Nobody has tried it. What everybody has tried is hiring her for the part she is not good at, and she has stopped letting them get away with it.
reference_stats.notes: Every advantage here is paired with a cost that is written in the species record rather than invented here, and the pairing is anatomical and commercial rather than mechanical. The bible gives the brine-and-fresh metabolism, the shallower sac, the two-chemistry kidney, the dialect intake and wide tolerance, the ceiling at eleven inherited from the salt parent with the water one changing nothing, the flat grinding teeth, and two statements that carry this whole character: that qi is noticeably slower than either parent in their own medium and that this is the cross's actual cost, and that range is not power. It also gives the senses - the best chemical sense in the record by a wide margin, because it must tell two waters apart at a glance, and it is always being lied to by one of them - and the reproduction, freely crossing both directions and never producing a stable parent type, because the tolerance is a tolerance and not a plan. All authored. What is mine is only the commercial consequence of the authored rate: that a trade which pays for speed is paying for the one thing her body does not sell. Nothing here invents a technique, a stat line or a rule of the game - no method of cultivation gives her either parent's speed, no item splits a sac that is in the wrong place, and no realm in the ladder is answered by being able to drink. The short version: she is the only body that is never stuck anywhere, and never being stuck is worth nothing on a run that buys speed.

art.palette_notes: Drift grey, sun ochre, wet slate, and a pale bloom of dried salt at every cuff and hairline. Deliberately two coasts in one frame: sun-dark on the windward side, damp and pale on the other. No jewellery - she has nothing that survives the crossing.
